meta.title: Directive (EU) 2016/1919 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 October 2016 on legal aid for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and for requested persons in European arrest warrant proceedings

items.heading: Article 1
items.comment: Provisions of the Directive on Legal Aid were transposed into the Croatian law through the amendments introduced into two pieces of national legislation: Criminal Procedure Act and the Act on Judicial Cooperation in Criminal Matters with the Member States of the European Union. Amendments of the latter were adopted in July 2019 and amendments of the latter were adopted in the December of the same year.

items.text: 1. This Directive lays down common minimum rules concerning the right to legal aid for:
(a)suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings; and
(b)persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings pursuant to Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA (requested persons).
2. This Directive complements Directives 2013/48/EU and (EU) 2016/800. Nothing in this Directive shall be interpreted as limiting the rights provided for in those Directives.
items.comment: Croatian law is in line with this provision of the Directive. The way that the Directive on legal aid was transposed into Croatian law did not limit the rights provided by Directives 2013/48/EU and (EU) 2016/800.

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. This Directive applies to suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings who have a right of access to a lawyer pursuant to Directive 2013/48/EU and who are:

items.comment: Croatian law fully transposes this provision of the Directive. The arrested person has the right to legal aid from the moment of the arrest. For other categories of persons who are deprived of liberty for the needs of criminal procedure – persons in custody and in pre-trial detention – provisions on mandatory defense apply. Provisions on mandatory defense in Croatian law have the same effect as the provisions on legal aid. The costs of mandatory defense are covered by the State. However, at the end of the proceedings, if the accused is found guilty, he/she may be ordered to cover the expenses of mandatory defense, if he/she has the means to do so.

provisions.comment: Croatia law grants the right to free legal aid to those suspects and accused persons who are required or permitted to participate in individual evidence-gathering actions. With regard to evidence gathering actions covered, Croatia law goes above the demands of the Directive because it grants the right to free legal aid also to those suspects and accused persons who are to be interrogated by the police, the investigator or the public prosecutor. However, Croatian law is not in line with the Directive because it limits this right only to those suspects and accused persons who are prosecuted for criminal offences for which a sentence of imprisonment of more than five years is prescribed.

items.comment: The Directive has not been officially transposed into Misdemeanors Act. Although the Misdemeanor Act stipulates that, where that law does not contain the relevant provisions on particular issues of procedure, the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Act will apply (Article 82(3)), it is difficult to assess whether this actually ensures the transposition of the provisions of the Directive. It remains to see what the research of practice will show with that regard.

items.text: (a)where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed or referred to such a court; or
(b)where deprivation of liberty cannot be imposed as a sanction;
this Directive applies only to the proceedings before a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters.
In any event, this Directive applies when a decision on detention is taken, and during detention, at any stage of the proceedings until the conclusion of the proceedings.
For the purposes of this Directive, ‘legal aid’ means funding by a Member State of the assistance of a lawyer, enabling the exercise of the right of access to a lawyer.
items.heading: Article 3
items.comment: In Croatia, Directive on legal aid has been transposed through 3 legal institutes - provisional legal assistance of a defence attorney at the expense of the budget, legal assistance of a defence attorney at the expense of the budget and mandatory defence. In all three cases, the costs of legal assistance are covered by the State. However, if, at the end of the proceedings, in a judgment in which the accused has been found guilty it is established that he has enough means to cover the costs of legal assistance, he/she will be obliged to do so.

items.heading: Article 4

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons who lack sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer have the right to legal aid when the interests of justice so require.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (19)
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (1) When the defense is not madatory, the defendant shall, at his request, upon receipt of the decision to carry out the investigation or the notification of conducting evidentiary actions referred to in Article 213, paragraph 2 of this Act, or after the indictment referred to in Article 341, paragraph 3 of this Act has been raised, until the final completion of criminal proceedings, appoint a defense attorney at the expense of budgetary resources, if he/she makes it probable that he/she is unable to cover his/her defense expenses without endangering his/her own dependency and the maintenance of his/her family or persons legally obliged to support, and complexity, severity or special circumstances of the case justify it.

provisions.comment: With regard to the arrested person, Croatian law applies the means test. There is a statutory presumption that in the case of the arrestee the merits test is fulfilled. With regard to suspects and accused persons who participate in individual evidence gathering actions, means test is applied. In the latter situation, merits test ius also applied, but there is a statutory presumption that the merits test is met only in case of criminal offences punishable by imprisonment of more than five years, which is contrary to the provisions of the Directive.
provisions.textEn:
(1) The arrestee referred to in Article 107, items 2 and 3 of this Law shall have the right to temporary legal assistance of a defense attorney at the expense of the budget from the moment of his arrest, as long as the arrest lasts, if he declares that he is unable to cover his defense expenses without endangering his own maintenance or maintenance of his family or persons he is legally required to support.

(2) The right to temporary legal assistance of defense counsel at the expense of the budget for individual actions, in proceedings conducted for criminal offenses for which a sentence of imprisonment of more than five years is prescribed, when the defense is mandatory, if he declares that according to his financial status he cannot cover the costs of defense without endangering his own dependency and the maintenance of his family or persons he is legally obliged to support, when taking the action in which he participates, also has:

1) the suspect referred to in Article 208a of this Law, who acquires this right before questioning by the police

2) a suspect who has acquired the status in accordance with Article 208, paragraph 5 of this Law, who acquires this right prior to questioning by the police

3) the suspect who participates in the evidentiary actions of recognizing, confronting, reconstructing the event, who acquires this right before taking the said actions

4) a suspect to be questioned before an indictment is filed in accordance with Article 341, paragraph 3 of this Act, which acquires this right before being examined by the state prosecutor or investigator

5) the suspect against whom ordering of pre-trial has been proposed, who acquires this right before holding a pre-trial detention hearing.

items.text: 2. Member States may apply a means test, a merits test, or both to determine whether legal aid is to be granted in accordance with paragraph 1.

provisions.comment: With regard to legal aid for accused persons, Croatian law applies both, the merits test and the means test.
provisions.textEn: 1) When the defense is not madatory, the defendant shall, at his request, upon receipt of the decision to carry out the investigation or the notification of conducting evidentiary actions referred to in Article 213, paragraph 2 of this Act, or after the indictment referred to in Article 341, paragraph 3 of this Act has been raised, until the final completion of criminal proceedings, appoint a defense attorney at the expense of budgetary resources, if he/she makes it probable that he/she is unable to cover his/her defense expenses without endangering his/her own dependency and the maintenance of his/her family or persons legally obliged to support, and complexity, severity or special circumstances of the case justify it.

provisions.comment: With regard to temporary legal assistance for suspects and accused persons, Croatian law applies both, the means test and the merits test.
provisions.textEn:
(1) The arrestee referred to in Article 107, items 2 and 3 of this Law shall have the right to temporary legal assistance of a defense attorney at the expense of the budget from the moment of his arrest, as long as the arrest lasts, if he declares that he is unable to cover his defense expenses without endangering his own maintenance or maintenance of his family or persons he is legally required to support.

(2) The right to temporary legal assistance of defense counsel at the expense of the budget for individual actions, in proceedings conducted for criminal offenses for which a sentence of imprisonment of more than five years is prescribed, when the defense is mandatory, if he declares that according to his financial status he cannot cover the costs of defense without endangering his own dependency and the maintenance of his family or persons he is legally obliged to support, when taking the action in which he participates, also has:

1) the suspect referred to in Article 208a of this Law, who acquires this right before questioning by the police

2) a suspect who has acquired the status in accordance with Article 208, paragraph 5 of this Law, who acquires this right prior to questioning by the police

3) the suspect who participates in the evidentiary actions of recognizing, confronting, reconstructing the event, who acquires this right before taking the said actions

4) a suspect to be questioned before an indictment is filed in accordance with Article 341, paragraph 3 of this Act, which acquires this right before being examined by the state prosecutor or investigator

5) the suspect against whom ordering of pre-trial has been proposed, who acquires this right before holding a pre-trial detention hearing.

items.text: 3. Where a Member State applies a means test, it shall take into account all relevant and objective factors, such as the income, capital and family situation of the person concerned, as well as the costs of the assistance of a lawyer and the standard of living in that Member State, in order to determine whether, in accordance with the applicable criteria in that Member State, a suspect or an accused person lacks sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer.

nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.comment: When applying the institute of the defense attorney at the expense of the budgetary funds, Croatian law applies the means test. The accused is required to make it probable that he/she is unable to cover his/her defense expenses without endangering his/her own dependency and the maintenance of his/her family or persons he/she is legally obliged to support. In order to show his financial situation he/she is required to submit evidence.
provisions.textEn:
1) When the defense is not madatory, the defendant shall, at his request, upon receipt of the decision to carry out the investigation or the notification of conducting evidentiary actions referred to in Article 213, paragraph 2 of this Act, or after the indictment referred to in Article 341, paragraph 3 of this Act has been raised, until the final completion of criminal proceedings, appoint a defense attorney at the expense of budgetary resources, if he/she makes it probable that he/she is unable to cover his/her defense expenses without endangering his/her own dependency and the maintenance of his/her family or persons legally obliged to support, and complexity, severity or special circumstances of the case justify it.

(2) The defendant shall file a reasoned request for the appointment of a defense attorney at the expense of budgetary funds before the State Attorney before the indictment is filed, or the court after the indictment is filed. In addition to the request, the defendant is obliged to enclose evidence of his financial status, the state of his family, or the persons he is legally required to support, or persons who are legally required to support him. Proof of assets must show total revenues within one year, data and account balances in banking and other financial institutions.

provisions.comment: When applying the institute of provisional legal assistance of a defence counsel at the expense of budgetary funds, Croatian law applies the means test. However, in order to fulfill this test, it is enough for the suspect or the accused person to make a statement that, owing to his/her financial situation, he/she is not able to cover the costs of legal assistance.
provisions.textEn:
(1) The arrestee referred to in Article 107, items 2 and 3 of this Law shall have the right to temporary legal assistance of a defense attorney at the expense of the budget from the moment of his arrest, as long as the arrest lasts, if he declares that he is unable to cover his defense expenses without endangering his own maintenance or maintenance of his family or persons he is legally required to support.

(2) The right to temporary legal assistance of defense counsel at the expense of the budget for individual actions, in proceedings conducted for criminal offenses for which a sentence of imprisonment of more than five years is prescribed, when the defense is mandatory, if he declares that according to his financial status he cannot cover the costs of defense without endangering his own dependency and the maintenance of his family or persons he is legally obliged to support, when taking the action in which he participates, also has:

1) the suspect referred to in Article 208a of this Law, who acquires this right before questioning by the police

2) a suspect who has acquired the status in accordance with Article 208, paragraph 5 of this Law, who acquires this right prior to questioning by the police

3) the suspect who participates in the evidentiary actions of recognizing, confronting, reconstructing the event, who acquires this right before taking the said actions

4) a suspect to be questioned before an indictment is filed in accordance with Article 341, paragraph 3 of this Act, which acquires this right before being examined by the state prosecutor or investigator

5) the suspect against whom ordering of pre-trial has been proposed, who acquires this right before holding a pre-trial detention hearing.

items.text: 4. Where a Member State applies a merits test, it shall take into account the seriousness of the criminal offence, the complexity of the case and the severity of the sanction at stake, in order to determine whether the interests of justice require legal aid to be granted. If the person has not been arrested, the right to legal aid is activated before the questioning by the police, public prosecutor or the investigator, or before individual evidence-gathering actions are carried out.

items.text: 6. Legal aid shall be granted only for the purposes of the criminal proceedings in which the person concerned is suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence.
items.comment: In Croatian law, legal aid is granted only for the purpose of the criminal proceedings in which the person concerned is suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Legal aid in European arrest warrant proceedings

items.text: 1. The executing Member State shall ensure that requested persons have a right to legal aid upon arrest pursuant to a European arrest warrant until they are surrendered, or until the decision not to surrender them becomes final.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o pravosudnoj suradnji s državama članicama Europske unije (19)
nationalActs.titleEn: Act on Amendments to the Act on Judicial Cooperation in Criminal Matters with the Member States of the European Union

provisions.comment: In Croatian law, upon arrest, the requested person is informed by the police that he/she has is entitled to a defense attorney in the Republic of Croatia, also when the defense is not mandatory, with the warning that the decision as to who will bear the costs of such a defense attorney will depend on the person's subsequently determined financial status. The purpose of this provision was to transpose the provisions of the Directive into Croatian law. However, this provision is not clear enough to be fully in line with the provisions of the Directive.
provisions.textEn: Upon arrest, the police will instruct the requested person that he/she is entitled to a defense attorney in the Republic of Croatia also when the defense is not mandatory, with the warning that the decision as to who will bear the costs of such a defense attorney will depend on the person's subsequently determined financial status.  If a European arrest warrant has been issued for the purpose of criminal prosecution, the police will inform the requested person upon arrest that he or she is entitled to request a lawyer in the issuing State. The police shall inform without delay the competent county court of the requested person's request for a defense attorney, who shall appoint the defense counsel. The police shall also inform the State Attorney's Office for the purpose of informing the competent authority of the issuing State of the request for a defense attorney in that state.

items.text: 2. The issuing Member State shall ensure that requested persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings for the purpose of conducting a criminal prosecution and who exercise their right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State to assist the lawyer in the executing Member State in accordance with Article 10(4) and (5) of Directive 2013/48/EU have the right to legal aid in the issuing Member State for the purpose of such proceedings in the executing Member State, in so far as legal aid is necessary to ensure effective access to justice.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Croatia has not transposed this provision. There is no right for the requested person who has appointed a lawyer in Croatia which acts as the issuing Member State to appoint a legal aid lawyer.

items.text: 3. The right to legal aid referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 may be subject to a means test in accordance with Article 4(3), which shall apply mutatis mutandis.

provisions.comment: Croatia applies a means test. However, the criteria for its application are not precisely prescribed by law.
provisions.textEn: Upon arrest, the police will instruct the requested person that he/she is entitled to a defense attorney in the Republic of Croatia also when the defense is not mandatory, with the warning that the decision as to who will bear the costs of such a defense attorney will depend on the person's subsequently determined financial status. If a European arrest warrant has been issued for the purpose of criminal prosecution, the police will inform the requested person upon arrest that he or she is entitled to request a lawyer in the issuing State. The police shall inform without delay the competent county court of the requested person's request for a defense attorney, who shall appoint the defense counsel. The police shall also inform the State Attorney's Office for the purpose of informing the competent authority of the issuing State of the request for a defense attorney in that state.

items.heading: Article 6
items.subHeading: Decisions regarding the granting of legal aid

items.text: 1. Decisions on whether or not to grant legal aid and on the assignment of lawyers shall be made, without undue delay, by a competent authority. Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that the competent authority takes its decisions diligently, respecting the rights of the defence.

nationalActs.title: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o kaznenom postupku (19)

provisions.comment: A decision to grant a request for a defence counsel at the expense of the budget is made by the public prosecutor, the president of the panel or the individual judge. If the decision was to grant a request, the defence counsel is assigned by the president of the court.
provisions.textEn:
(4) The decision on the appointment of a defence counsel at the expense of the budget shall be made by a reasoned ruling issued by the public prosecutor or the president of the panel or an individual judge, who, if he/she deems it necessary, may first check or obtain additional information on the financial status of the defendant, his/her family and persons referred to in paragraph 2 of this article. The appeal against the decision of the public prosecutor is decided by the judge of investigation, while the decision on the appeal against the decision of the president of the panel or an individual judge is decided by the panel.

(6) The President of the court shall appoint the defense counsel by decision. No appeal against this decision is allowed. If the defendant has previously exercised the right to temporary legal assistance referred to in Article 72a of this Act, the same lawyer shall, as a rule, be appointed as a defense counsel at the expense of the budget.

items.heading: Article 7
items.subHeading: Quality of legal aid services and training

items.text: 1. Member States shall take necessary measures, including with regard to funding, to ensure that:

nationalActs.title: Pravilnik o visini nagrade odvjetniku određenom za brenitelja po službenoj dužnosti
nationalActs.titleEn: Regulation on the amount of remuneration for a lawyer appointed ex officio

provisions.comment: The fact that the lawyer appointed ex officio (including a legal aid lawyer) receives only 30 percent of the remuneration he/she would be entitled to as a chosen lawyer affects the quality of the legal aid in a negative way.
provisions.textEn: The remuneration of the defense lawyer appointed ex officio shall be set at 30% of the remuneration for which the lawyer would be entitled to certain actions in the procedure under the Tariff on Remuneration and Compensation for the Attorney's Work (Official Gazette 148/09).

nationalActs.title: Zakon o kaznenom postupku
nationalActs.titleEn: Criminal Procedure Act

provisions.textEn: (4) Only a lawyer may be taken as a defense attorney, and a lawyer may be replaced by a lawyer trainee who has passed the bar examination in proceedings before a municipal court for offenses for which a fine or imprisonment of up to five years is prescribed. Before a county court, a lawyer can only be a lawyer. In proceedings for a criminal offense for which long-term imprisonment is prescribed, only a lawyer who has a practice of at least eight years as a lawyer or as an official in a judicial body may be a lawyer ex officio or at the expense of budgetary resources.

items.text: (a)there is an effective legal aid system that is of an adequate quality; and
(b)legal aid services are of a quality adequate to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, with due respect for the independence of the legal profession.
2. Member States shall ensure that adequate training is provided to staff involved in the decision-making on legal aid in criminal proceedings and in European arrest warrant proceedings.

3. With due respect for the independence of the legal profession and for the role of those responsible for the training of lawyers, Member States shall take appropriate measures to promote the provision of adequate training to lawyers providing legal aid services.

4. Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have the right, upon their request, to have the lawyer providing legal aid services assigned to them replaced, where the specific circumstances so justify.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of their rights under this Directive.

items.heading: Article 9

provisions.comment: In deciding on the need to appoint a defence counsel at the expense of the budget, special circumstance of the case are also taken into consideration. These special circumstances include individual circumstance of the suspect or the accused person, including his/her vulnerability.
provisions.textEn: 1) When the defense is not madatory, the defendant shall, at his request, upon receipt of the decision to carry out the investigation or the notification of conducting evidentiary actions referred to in Article 213, paragraph 2 of this Act, or after the indictment referred to in Article 341, paragraph 3 of this Act has been raised, until the final completion of criminal proceedings, appoint a defense attorney at the expense of budgetary resources, if he/she makes it probable that he/she is unable to cover his/her defense expenses without endangering his/her own dependency and the maintenance of his/her family or persons legally obliged to support, and complexity, severity or special circumstances of the case justify it.
